Elation

/i-LAY-shun/ — rhymes with station · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Elation is a feeling of intense joy and excitement.

She jumped with elation when the college acceptance letter arrived.

Worked Example

She felt unmistakable elation when the acceptance letter arrived from her dream college, dancing around the room and shouting with joy.

Elation is the precise word here because it captures not just happiness but the explosive, exuberant joy that has to burst out physically. Happiness would miss the sense of overwhelming excitement that can't be contained.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

delight: Delight is lively pleasure you take in a particular thing — a fireworks show, a clever gift, a good meal. It stays pleasant and manageable. Elation is far bigger: a soaring burst of triumphant joy, usually after a major success, so strong it makes you want to jump and shout.

euphoria: Euphoria is an overwhelming, almost floating wave of happiness that can wash over you with no obvious trigger at all. Elation is just as intense but tied to a reason — an acceptance letter, a championship win. If the joy comes from a definite triumph, it is elation.

glee: Glee is bright, bubbling merriment that often spills out in giggles — sometimes over something small or even mischievous. Elation is grander and more triumphant: the soaring joy of a big success. A prank can fill you with glee; a college acceptance brings elation.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

despair: total loss of hope and spirit

dejection: low-spirited sadness that weighs you down

Where it sits · how high the spirits soar — sadness → contentment → joy → elation

sadness vs. elation: Sadness sits at the opposite end of the scale from elation: sadness drags the spirit down, while elation sends it soaring with intense, jump-for-joy excitement.

contentment vs. elation: Contentment is far milder than elation — contentment is a quiet, settled satisfaction, while elation is a sudden burst of thrilled, soaring happiness.

joy vs. elation: Joy is strong happiness, but elation is stronger still: joy warms you from inside, while elation lifts you so high you might literally jump and shout.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e- (ex-)

Prefix — e- (ex-): out, up from (Latin)

Root — lat (latus)

Root — lat (latus): carried, borne (Latin)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or state of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: E- means 'out, up,' lat- means 'carried,' and -ion turns it into a state — so elation is literally the state of being 'carried up,' which is exactly how intense joy feels: lifted right off the ground.

Use the root in a new word: translate

Use the root in a new word: translate: To translate a book is to 'carry it across' into another language — the same Latin root lat- ('carried') that makes elation the feeling of being carried up with joy.

Word Choice

neutral / literary

Reach for elation when someone experiences a peak moment of exuberant triumph—an acceptance letter, a championship win, a life-changing yes. It captures the sense that joy has become so intense it bursts out physically. For milder happiness, the simpler word 'happiness' or 'pleasure' usually fits better.
